question.prompt: Line \(a\) is parallel to plane \(\alpha\). A plane containing \(a\) intersects \(\alpha\) along \(b\). What follows?

solutions.explanation: This is a property of a line parallel to a plane: the line of intersection is parallel to the original line.
solutions.title: Apply the property theorem

solutions.explanation: Both \(a\) and \(b\) lie in the cutting plane, so they are coplanar. Since \(a\parallel\alpha\), no point of \(a\) lies in \(\alpha\). But \(b\) lies in \(\alpha\), so \(a\) and \(b\) have no common point. Coplanar lines with no common point are parallel. Thus \(a\parallel b\), choice C.
solutions.title: Use coplanarity and nonintersection
